items.title: Trump says 'deep state' officials will be charged in speech claiming voter fraud
items.description: US President Donald Trump uses a presidential speech to accuse China of improperly trying to influence the 2020 election and stop him from winning the presidency.

items.title: Trump's speech a desperate move — and 'ominous sign' ahead of midterms
items.description: Using a prime-time address to the nation to repeat long-debunked claims about the 2020 election defeat is a desperate and unusual move. Analysts say it's an "ominous sign" of how Donald Trump may handle the upcoming midterms.

items.title: Universities were told of risks from violent intruders at campus protests
items.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion has heard the tertiary sector's peak standards body wrote to universities to warn them about aggressive outsiders infiltrating pro-Palestinian protests.

items.title: No guarantee outages won't happen again, Telstra CEO says
items.description: The national Telstra outage last week was triggered by maintenance work that caused the system's clocks to go back two decades, the telco says.

items.title: PNG ousts Taiwan officials, seeks to 'reassure' China after Australian treaty
items.description: Papua New Guinea will close Taiwan's trade mission in the country, freezing out its fifth largest trading partner in a major strategic move designed to reaffirm ties with China.

items.title: Landslide buries people, destroys buildings in south-western China
items.description: A landslide in south-western China's Chongqing municipality has buried people in rubble and destroyed a roadway and a number of buildings, according to state media.

items.title: Taking violence seriously is more complex than a royal commission
items.description: Experts are divided about whether there should be a royal commission into violence against women but say the solutions to the problem are already known and need funding.

items.title: Hanson laments end of White Australia policy on Tommy Robinson podcast
items.description: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has blamed the end of the White Australia policy for migration issues in the country during a controversial podcast appearance with a far-right activist in the UK.

items.title: US strikes bridges and collapses tower at port in Iran campaign
items.description: The United States expanded its air strike campaign against Iran early Friday by hitting more bridges and apparently collapsing a tower at a key Iranian port.

items.title: NSW woman arrested as part of Dezi Freeman investigation
items.description: A NSW woman was arrested in Bairnsdale today as part of Victoria Police's investigation into the movements of dead police killer Dezi Freeman.

items.title: Live: Big miners BHP and Rio Tinto dive as investors fret about investment outlook
items.description: BHP Group's investors are in a world of pain today. It follows Thursday's operational update from the miner. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: 'Carry on patriots': Trump officials defend pilot after fighter jet stunt
items.description: Officials, including US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, continue to support low-altitude military flyovers despite growing safety concerns after a jet was filmed buzzing a crowded beach.  Trump administration officials have backed the manoeuvre, with the White House posting a cartoon of the stunt along with the words "it's okay to love America". Similar flights have previously come under review but were dismissed by the Pentagon.

items.title: Treasurer says AI key to raising productivity, lowering interest rates
items.description: The Treasurer has given an insight into his April meeting with Anthropic, arguing that Australia embracing AI is crucial for turning around the nation's lacklustre productivity and economic performance over recent decades.

items.title: Australia's number one song now has AI credits on Spotify
items.description: DJ and music producer Josh Fawaz has updated the song credits on Spotify on his viral track Like a Prayer. Generative AI drums and vocals are now credited.

items.title: Toilet germs and other things living in your make-up brushes
items.description: Various studies have shown that make-up tools, including brushes, can harbour a range of bacteria, including opportunistic pathogens.

items.title: Will Ferrell channels Ricky Bobby in TV return
items.description: Plus a noir mystery set in outback Coober Pedy, a true crime drama which doesn't exploit its victims, and more new TV to watch this month.

items.title: Decade-long friendship between Roy Orbison's hit maker and Australian singer
items.description: Every Monday morning for the last 14 years, Australian musician Damien Leith has been meeting with the late Joe Melson, the Nashville songwriter responsible for some of Roy Orbison's biggest hits.

items.title: Parents go against court orders after children 'traumatised'
items.description: The Family Court granted John full custody of his kids, but he returned them to their mother, saying the judge got it wrong.

items.title: Uber reverses 'disability tax' after outcry
items.description: Uber has reversed its decision to impose a $5 fee on passengers requiring extra assistance, after advocates and service providers labelled it discriminatory and a "disability tax".

items.title: UK urges FIFA to act after Argentine players hold up Malvinas banner
items.description: The British government urges FIFA to investigate after Argentine players held up a banner declaring the Falkland Islands were Argentinian.

items.title: Ex-Wagga MP Daryl Maguire found guilty of conspiracy over fraudulent visas
items.description: After five days of deliberation in the NSW District Court the former Member for Wagga Wagga was found to have conspired to provide false or misleading information to the Commonwealth on visas for Chinese nationals seeking permanent residency.

items.title: Drivers wait months for faults to be repaired on EVs built by new brands
items.description: As an influx of car brands enters the market, dealers ask for a change to consumer laws to fix a grey area that makes them responsible for warranty repairs.

items.title: 'People want something different': Ardern on the rise of fringe politics
items.description: The former New Zealand prime minister reflects on leading through crisis, becoming a mother while running a country and why she believes voters are craving something different.

items.title: Sam Neill died from a common infection. Here's how it turned deadly
items.description: After the actor's death from pneumonia, here's what to know about the common infection, its symptoms and why it can sometimes become deadly.

items.title: Bus driver found guilty over fatal CBD crash appeals conviction
items.description: Lindsay Francis Selby was found guilty last year of driving without due care and attention when he struck and killed Tia Cameron in 2024.
